1.name: Axle housing
1.note: The cast banjo that holds the whole drive and the oil bath. Every bearing in the sheet sits in it, so it carries the gear loads to the car.

2.name: Rear cover
2.note: Pressed steel lid that closes the back of the housing and keeps the oil in.

3.name: Hex screw
3.note: Clamps the rear cover to the housing flange.

4.name: Axle tube
4.note: Steel tube pressed into each side of the housing. It encloses the half-shaft and carries the wheel bearing.

5.name: Drive pinion
5.note: Takes the propshaft's turning through a right angle by meshing with the crown wheel. It is the single input to the differential.

6.name: Pinion bearing, outer
6.note: Taper roller bearing that carries the pinion's radial and axial thrust at the flange end.

7.name: Pinion bearing, inner
7.note: The second taper roller bearing, spaced from the first so the pinion stays rigid under load.

8.name: Collapsible spacer
8.note: A crushable sleeve between the two pinion bearings. Tightening the nut squeezes it, which sets the bearing preload.

9.name: Shaft seal
9.note: Lip seal on the pinion shaft. It keeps the oil in and the dirt out.

10.name: Companion flange
10.note: Splined to the pinion. The propshaft bolts to it, so all the engine's torque enters here.

11.name: Pinion nut
11.note: Holds the flange on the pinion and, by crushing the spacer, sets the bearing preload.

12.name: Crown wheel
12.note: The large bevel gear driven by the pinion. It turns the carrier, so it is where the single input splits into two outputs.

13.name: Hex bolt
13.note: Fixes the crown wheel to the carrier flange so they turn as one.

14.name: Differential carrier
14.note: The cage that holds the cross pin, spiders and side gears. It always turns at the mean of the two wheel speeds.

15.name: Carrier bearing
15.note: A taper roller bearing on each end of the carrier, letting it spin in the housing while taking the crown wheel's thrust.

16.name: Shim pack
16.note: Thin shims behind each carrier bearing. They set the preload and the crown wheel's backlash against the pinion.

17.name: Side gear
17.note: One per half-shaft, splined to it. Each side gear is an output, and the spiders push equally on both, which splits the torque equally.

18.name: Thrust washer
18.note: A bronze washer behind each side gear that takes its axial thrust against the carrier.

19.name: Spider gear
19.note: Bevel gear that links the two side gears. It stays still on its pin when the wheels match and spins when they differ, as in a turn.

20.name: Spherical washer
20.note: A domed bronze washer behind each spider gear that takes its outward thrust against the carrier.

21.name: Cross pin
21.note: The axle the spider gears turn on. It rides round with the carrier.

22.name: Spring pin
22.note: Locks the cross pin in the carrier so it cannot slide out.

23.name: Half-shaft
23.note: Carries each side gear's turning out to its wheel. These are the two outputs that may run at different speeds.

24.name: Ball bearing
24.note: Sealed ball bearing at the outer end of each axle tube, supporting the half-shaft near the wheel.

25.name: Wheel stud
25.note: Pressed into the half-shaft flange. The wheel is clamped on them with nuts.
